text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar repeatedly rejected ideas about devaluation of the crown, saying the currency was and would be stable.
- Meciar said Slovakia's economic potential may enable the country to fulfil the Maastricht criteria as the first post-communist state, or even faster than some EU countries.
- The regulation of energy prices is expected to last at least until the year 2000. Deregulation is expected to double the current prices.
- Steel producer VSZ has denied reports that it was interested in purchasing the independent daily Pravda.

HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The Slovak Antimonopoly Bureau reviewed 129 cases in the first eight months of this year, most of which were on abusing a dominant market position. Fines imposed by the bureau totalled 2.4 milliom crowns in January- August period.

- According to a public opinion poll, 30 percent of citizens have not yet decided what to do with their privatisation bonds. About 28 percent said they would keep the bond until its maturity date in the year 2001, and 20 percent want to sell their bond before its maturity.
PRAVDA - Increasing tension in a junior member of the ruling coalition, the ultra-left Workers Party, will result in reducing the number of coalition deputies to 79 from 82.

- The Antimonopoly Bureau said it was reviewing steel maker VSZ's activities aimed at acquiring control of several Slovak banks, but that the VSZ so far had not violated the competition law. The bureau said VSZ might attempt to gain majority stakes in banks through its subsidiaries, and that it would also review their activities.
SME - The National Property Fund (NPF), the state privatisation agency, has approved privatisation of another 23 companies. Details of the sales should be available today.
